pcs.pc_description: use pressure relief valves and automatic shut- off mechanisms to prevent the uncontrolled release of hydrogen
utilize oil-free equipment compatible with pure oxygen to avoid combustion risks
choose electrical equipment rated for zone 0 or zone 1 depending on the potential hydrogen concentration and risk of spark ignition
set up intrinsically safe tools and components that eliminate the risk of sparking, such as sealed switches, capacitors, and motors
implement various control measures, such as pressure relief valves, explosion suppression systems, leak detection systems, interlocks and automated safety systems
install various hydrogen flame detection methods, such as Ultraviolet (UV) Flame Detectors, Infrared (IR) Flame Detectors, Multi-spectrum Detectors, Video Image Flame Detectors (VIFDs), etc.
use sensors that can alert the responsible person such as a safety officer when storage rooms are not maintaining the ideal conditions for storing hazardous chemicals

check the tank farm for adherence to various regulations and mandatory compliances required
use checklists for commissioning of each hydrogen system / equipment / machinery / piping as per OEM recommendation
perform pre-operative tests of tanks, pipelines, valves, regulators, control systems, fire safety equipment, alarms etc.
ensure all the equipment and control systems clear the pre-operative tests as per guidelines and regulations, else take corrective actions
perform trial run and pre -commissioning tests in accordance with the applicable norms/ statutory requirement/ regulatory standards
provide final go-ahead for commissioning once the components are fully tested and required approvals are received

modules.module_title: Compliance with GH2 Regulations and Standards

pcs.pc_description: stay informed about the latest regulations related to hydrogen production, storage and refuelling
keep away any ignition sources from hydrogen storage areas and maintain a strict no- smoking policy within this zone
ensure hazardous areas and equipment are clearly marked with appropriate signage and warnings

use specialized Personal Protective Equipment (PPE) for working in a hydrogen environment, such as flame-resistant suits made from non-static material, goggles and face shields to protect against pressure-driven debris, gloves (neoprene or nitrile), safety boots, respirators and hearing protection for noisy areas
always wear appropriate cryogenic protective clothing, gloves and equipment when handling liquid hydrogen
report any non-compliance issues promptly to relevant personnel
liaise with regulatory authorities during inspections and audits
prepare written accident/incident report and share with the concerned officer/department
inform fire safety department about any near- miss incidents in the work place
adhere to safety protocols when using materials, tools, and equipment for handling GH2
refer to relevant safety standards and guidelines like IEC 61508, NFPA 2, and industry best practices for identifying hydrogen process hazards
vent hydrogen to a safe, designated area well away from ignition sources, using a dedicated vent stack designed for high-pressure hydrogen release
dilute oxygen with an inert gas like nitrogen before venting to decrease its concentration and mitigate fire risks
check that pathways/ emergency escape routes are clear and free from grease/ oil and ensure good housekeeping practices
maintain ideal temperature and humidity level of storage areas used to safely contain gas cylinders and follow infection control guidelines
follow first aid instructions according to the type of injury/ incident
move yourself or the injured person away from the source of the cryogenic liquid or gas to stop further exposure

modules.module_title: Emergency, Disaster and Pollution control response

pcs.pc_description: review and approve disaster management plans, drill schedules shared by supervisors
raise alarms in case of any emergency - fire, leakage, or pollution
use appropriate fire extinguishers compatible with hydrogen and fire hoses to isolate the fire at the source
wear appropriate personal protective equipment (PPE) when handling or using extinguishers in a hydrogen environment
operate emergency shutdown procedures in case of leaks, pressure spikes, or other safety concerns and activate alarms as necessary
respond promptly and effectively to emergencies and potential hydrogen leaks, including evacuation procedures, communication with emergency services, and implementation of emergency response plans
coordinate with local authorities and nearby village representatives for evacuation
follow SOP to contain the disaster or pollution
assist fellow workers in quick response and evacuation as per SOP
